recipes.name: Quinoa Black Bean Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 teaspoon hot pepper sauce (such as Frank's RedHot®)

steps.text: Bring water and quinoa to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until quinoa is tender and water has been absorbed, about 15 to 20 minutes.

Roughly mash black beans with a fork, leaving some whole, to form a paste-like mixture. Mix quinoa, bread crumbs, bell pepper, egg, onion, garlic, cumin, hot pepper sauce, and salt into black beans using your hands. Form into 5 patties.
Add olive oil to a large skillet and heat on medium.
Cook patties until heated through and lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Quinoa Black Bean Burgers
raw_recipe.description: Vegetarian quinoa-black bean burgers are easy, quick, and delicious served on a whole wheat bun with garlic-lemon mayo, spinach, tomato, and onions.

review.reviewBody: This is the best vegetarian burger I've ever made! When I cook with quinoa, I usually use 1 part Quinoa to 2 parts water, so I double-checked the website where this recipe originated. It calls for 3/4 cup cooked quinoa, so you might want to adjust your recipe accordingly. Definitely worth a try!

I used 3/4 of a cup of quinoa and got 8 regular sized patties, but I actually think 1/2 cup of quinoa is enough. I put them in the oven at 400 for 30 min. and they came out crunchy and tasty. I did not have yellow bell pepper so I used tomato, and garlic powder since I did not have garlic either. This recipe is very forgiving in terms of ingredients.

I loved it. I doubled the recipe, added a carrot, onion power, garlic power and 2 jalapeños. I baked them on 350 for 25 minutes, because I wanted to freeze them. The ones I ate I sprinkled a little olive and juice from a lime over the top. They were easy to make and now I have them in the freezer for another time.

My girlfriend and I loved this recipe but, like with all others, I add or modify them, so I recommend the following because these turned out fantastic: 

Add an extra half tbsp of cumin, 1/2 tbsp of cracked black pepper, 1/4 Lea & Perrins, saute the sweet onion with brown sugar, and grille them. rather than pan-fry.

Finally, I topped these babies with Dubliner Irish Cheddar cheese and a hefty amount of crushed red pepper, along with mustard and ketchup, on whole wheat buns.

Definitely a repeat dinner!

Fantastic flavor. I mixed everything in the food processor then refrigerated the mixture for 30 minutes. I used my pattie press to avoid a bulky burger. I grilled them for 8 minutes a side as recommended on an indoor smokeless grill. They did not fall apart and were just perfect! I followed the recipe exactly except my husband is allergic to bell peppers so I left them out.

This is a very forgiving recipe! I used it as a base for what I had on hand. I used about 1c quinoa, mashed can of black beans, small can of corn and swapped the breadcrumbs for oatmeal per suggestion. I also added in some green onions from The garden along with the spices and egg it called for. I could not get these to Stay together so I scooped and compacted the filling in a 1/3c measuring cup and made the Patty's that way. Grilled and they tasted very tasty! I would suggest upping the spice if not using the breadcrumbs as it could use a little more salt with using the oats! Good base to play around with for what you have on hand!

It made a tasty, pasty something that didn’t resemble the taste or texture of a burger at all. I scrambled up 1/4 of a “patty” with an egg, added 1T salsa and 1T sour cream, wrapped it up in a tortilla and it made a very tasty breakfast burrito 😎

Easy to follow recipe. I did add more garlic than called for along with basil and parsley. Also added a diced beet. Put on the BBQ for a lettuce wrapped burger with tomato, more onion (raw) a bit of guacamole! I believe next time I'll add some cheese while grilling. I did read a couple of reviews on how dry the patties were. I don't know what I did differently but they were moist with each bite.

Delish! Someone in my house doesn't care for black beans or bell pepper so I subbed the for white beans, omitted the bell peppers, and added a splash of soy sauce. This was so so good. I am planning on making a big batch to freeze for a quick meal. They do fall apart a bit but bean burgs are kind of just like that. Add more moisture if it's too much and you are good to go. 👍🏻

As a basic recipe this one is okay -- it hits the major ingredients and proportions. But it's pretty bland both in terms of texture and spice. I used another clove of garlic, more cumin, and instead of hot sauce used medium chili powder (and salt and pepper). I also sautéed the onion (and used twice as much as the recipe calls for) and garlic and the pepper before adding and some frozen corn to the mix. I made these patties and let them rest in the fridge for a couple of hours until I was ready to cook them and then pressed both sides into some panko bread crumbs before frying as directed.

I Had been looking for a black bean burger recipe - tried several and this is a keeper! Just the right consistency and the peppers and onion add a nice crunch.

I had quinoa left over that I had cooked with vegetable broth so it was very flavorful. I used panko bread crumbs. I did not fry these but used an olive oil spray on a cast iron pan so they cooked very quickly.

Served it with hummus and avocado.

Have shared with several friends already.

Great healthy alternative to a cheeseburger! I love the flavor profile. I used organic white quinoa and gluten-free/dairy-free bread crumbs. These patties stayed together beautifully without any chilling or freezing.
I'm trying to avoid processed foods so InstaPotted my black beans and then mixed them in. A great recipe although the patties didn't hold together. We crumble it up and use it for tacos.
Absolutely great! We added mushrooms, green onion and dried cayenne peppers

I made this with a 6 bean medley instead of black beans, and I also added a few tablespoons of vital wheat gluten to made the dough more meaty. The burgers were fantastic. We gobbled them right up and I will definitely make them again:)
It was very tasty! We will definitely be eating this again.
So good! And quite easy to make

I have made these burgers several times now, each time changing up the seasoning but keeping the base of the quinoa and black beans. I will sometimes have to add an additional egg. I made them tonight and they came out great! I did not use the peppers or the cumin or the hot sauce, but instead used coriander, onion and garlic powder, mushroom powder, and smoked paprika. I always cook them in avocado oil. These are my go-to veggie burger and I appreciate the recipe! Thanks!
